question.worked_solution:
To find the common ratio $r$ of a geometric sequence given two terms ${a}_{m}$ and ${a}_{n},$ we use the formula

$$
{r}^{n-m}=\frac{{a}_{n}}{{a}_{m}}.
$$

In this case, we're given ${a}_{9}=-\frac{3}{25}$ and ${a}_{6}=-15.$ Substituting $n=9$ and $m=6$ into the formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{9-6} & =\frac{{a}_{9}}{{a}_{6}} \\ {r}^{3} & =\frac{(-\frac{3}{25})}{(-15)} \\ {r}^{3} & =\frac{1}{125}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by solving the equation for $r,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{3} & =\frac{1}{125} \\ {r}^{3} & ={(\frac{1}{5})}^{3} \\ r & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
